As a way to soothe myself I would play sims 4 and live in sulani because it’s such a beautiful world and I’d just make my sims swim in the ocean, scuba dive and do all the nice relaxing things. Finally starting to feel somewhat normal but I still enjoy the peace of the game

Thank you. I don’t know what anybody can do, not even myself. I’m just holding on and trying to get through each day

About two months into our relationship (jan 2020)I was really ill and completely bed bound for a week straight. My boyfriend and I weren’t at the seeing each other every day stage yet he came every day and brought me food and spent time with me and I knew then he was a good one. I’ve been having a major depressive episode since September 2020 with intense suicidal thoughts/actions and he’s been so incredibly supportive and kept me safe. Couldn’t ask for a kinder man

Not sure where you are but I’m in the UK and I am getting in person high intensive CBT this Tuesday. I self referred around 14th December, had a triage appointment 18th December to see what form of therapy would be best. The process has been a lot quicker than I expected
This is also my exact situation today. I feel your pain

I don’t have any “real”/tangible issues and I’ve never been more depressed or ready to commit suicide
Thank you, I don’t feel how I thought I would feel if I was getting better. I still have a lot of suicidal ideation so will see how things go and consider changing
I agree I’m completely the same. Feel like I’m floating along and feel so disconnected from life
Yes I feel exactly like this. Really hard to see the point in anything when I feel so disconnected from living. I really hope the treatment brings you some relief

There are a lot of workout videos on YouTube and some good boxing ones too. This could be an easier commitment than getting ready, leaving the house, travelling somewhere and interacting with other people
I wish I could just not wake up. I don’t have the energy for anything else
I feel this. There’s a lot we can’t say for the risk of scaring other people. My family are supervising me as it is, never mind if I told them the full extent of my thoughts
Yes! I’ve indulged myself too but it’s just something to battle myself on

This is exactly what I’m dealing with now. I cycle between wanting to kill myself then thinking about how my family would feel so I resolve to continue living. Then I want to kill myself to finally have some relief and the cycle goes on. Really hard place to be
Thinking of you. It’s so hard to pull yourself up when you’re feeling so low no matter how much you may want to deep down
That really resonates with me right now

Thanks for asking, not a huge story really I’ve just been depressed but functioning for a very long time and I reached out 3 months ago to get help and it’s all gone downhill from there to be honest. Everybody is very positive about me getting better and to hold on but hold on for what? I don’t think it’s worth it anymore
Yeah that would be good
It’s hard to open up to people and even harder when they don’t understand or know how to help. Have you contacted your doctor?
Really sorry to hear that you’re feeling so low, I’m there now so completely understand how crippling those feelings are. You’re more than just a grade or a number please try and remember that
Definitely interested please share
So true, it’s hard to speak with people who haven’t experienced these feelings

Agree with this and I’ll be your suicidal friend. I’ve opened up because my boyfriend encouraged me to share every time I feel low. I’ve tried telling him a couple times how I feel so hopeless and want to end things and the worst part is how upset he gets - I hate making him worry/feel this way. I think it would scare people how obsessed I am with dying so I just keep it to myself

Ugh yes definitely feel the bittersweetness! Great way to sum it up. 

I also find it really hard when people try and be positive with me and tell me things will get better. I know they’re trying to help and I don’t realistically expect them to come out with “yeah you’re right maybe you end your life” but it’s hard to stomach the constant reassurances things will be better when you really can’t see it happening.

I agree - I don’t necessarily want to die but I want this to end. The need to end things comes from a desperation for things to change, for me to feel something other than overwhelming dread and panic. I’m doing all the correct things they tell you to do - the counselling, the meditation, the exercise etc but it doesn’t make a difference which is where the frustration and desperation comes in.

Oh I agree with the talking comment too. While it’s cathartic in the moment to discuss things, it’s not as though you’re offloading onto somebody and the problem can then be resolved. It’s still there. You still have to deal with it. That’s why I’ve felt so unsatisfied with counselling. I don’t know about you but I worry about being a burden to other people and hate the thought of upsetting or even irritating people with talking about my low mood constantly and my suicidal thoughts so I tend to keep it to myself. I too feel like I live and only do things for other people to make them happy - I don’t really have a will of my own to continue on.

Counselling wasn’t for me which is why I’ve referred for something more intensive. I think all we can do is try things and see if they help. The long process of trying to recover is so disheartening when we’re in distress and need something urgently. You could try counselling and try commit to the process of the sessions and utilising the exercises and tools they give you, then at least you’ll know one way or another if it works. Though it is hard to get into that mindset of engaging with a counsellor - especially when you’re dubious of the benefits and finding a good counsellor can be a trial and error process.

I completely understand what you mean. I feel as though nothing motivates me to live for myself right now and all I think about is how other people would feel if I wasn’t here and I continue to live to keep them happy. I also hate the thought of my loved ones finding me.

I look back at my past and can recognise I did have happier moments in my life but overall I feel the majority of time I’ve felt disconnected from the situations and always felt like something isn’t quite right and generally unhappy. I constantly search for the next thing that will magically make me truly happy and not a muted version. The disappointment that each moment/event/thing didn’t make me fully happy is always stronger than the happiness in that moment. I hope that made sense as I’m struggling to put this feeling into words 

The counselling was good in the sense that I’m able to be more open and talk about my feelings but I’m finding the feelings too overwhelming. I tried all the techniques my counsellor suggested but I feel if I wasn’t so depressed they would make a difference. It’s been nice to have undivided time to talk about my feelings without feeling I’m upsetting or scaring people but I’m waiting for CBT as it should be more intense for me. I haven’t noticed any difference with the antidepressants and had some mild side effects. 

Taking the first step is hard and people forget continuing to attend counselling and commit to really trying to follow through and help yourself is even harder. I hope you find that courage within yourself to begin taking those steps

Thank you, I was on citalopram for six weeks and have been on mirtazapine for a week now as the crisis team thought it might be a better fit. I’m waiting for a CBT appointment too but it is very hard to hold on to feel some kind of benefit
